description: Holds account transfer sub header records, linked to account transfer main header.
business_purpose: Used to track and report account transfer sub header records for the Accounts & Finance area.
record_granularity: One row represents one account transfer sub header.

columns.name: Id
columns.description: Unique identifier of the account transfer sub header.

columns.name: SubHeaderName
columns.description: Sub header name of the account transfer sub header.

columns.name: AccountTransferMainHeaderId
columns.description: Reference to the account transfer main header linked to this account transfer sub header.

columns.name: created_byId
columns.description: User who created the account transfer sub header.

columns.name: created_date
columns.description: Date and time when the record was created.

columns.name: modified_byId
columns.description: User who last modified the account transfer sub header.

columns.name: modified_date
columns.description: Date and time when the record was last modified.

columns.name: is_deleted
columns.description: Soft-delete flag. True when the record has been deleted.

columns.name: is_default
columns.description: True when the account transfer sub header is default.

relationships.description: Each account transfer sub header references one account transfer main header (account transfer main header).
User who created the account transfer sub header.
User who last modified the account transfer sub header.
Each account transfer sub header can have many account transfer records referencing it through sub_headId.

business_rules: Deleted records (is_deleted = 1) should normally be excluded from reporting.
created_date is the preferred date column for period-based reporting.
Join to Account Transfer Main Header through the foreign key columns to resolve names.
common_queries: Account Transfer Sub Header by month
Account Transfer Sub Header by account transfer main header

query_notes: The database is MySQL/MariaDB; use MySQL syntax and the exact name AccountTransferSubHeader (identifiers can be case-sensitive).
Always filter is_deleted = 0 unless deleted records are explicitly requested.
Use COUNT(DISTINCT Id) when counting account transfer sub header records; joins can duplicate rows.
To resolve names, join on: AccountTransferMainHeaderId = AccountTransferMainHeader.Id.
